meta.title: DecisionGuard AI · Risk analysis before you decide
meta.description: Analyze, anticipate and monitor the risks of your strategic decisions with verified multi-agent AI.

hero.subtitle: You describe a decision. Seven agents each examine it from one angle: finance, strategy, law, cybersecurity, people, operations and scenarios. An eighth checks their work before anything reaches your report.

agents.title: Eight agents, one file.
agents.intro: Each stays in its own field and asks its own questions. No conclusion leaves without going through the auditor.

list.name: Finance
list.body: Cash flow, debt, profitability, return on investment, budget overruns.

list.name: Strategy
list.body: Positioning, competition, reputation, dependencies and long-term consequences.

list.name: Legal & compliance
list.body: GDPR, OHADA law, contracts, employment law. It flags issues; it does not replace your lawyer.

list.name: Cybersecurity & technology
list.body: Threats, data breaches, software dependencies, system availability.

list.name: People & organisation
list.body: Hiring, skills, resistance to change, management capacity.

list.name: Operations
list.body: Suppliers, logistics, lead times, business continuity.

list.name: Scenarios
list.body: Optimistic, realistic, pessimistic, crisis: what changes when assumptions change.

agents.auditBody: It compares what the other agents say, redoes the calculations and checks sources and their dates. When a conclusion does not hold, it sends it back with a specific request.

method.title: From the first draft to the report you sign.

steps.title: We ask the right questions
steps.body: When essential information is missing, DecisionGuard asks for it instead of assuming.

steps.title: Agents analyse in parallel
steps.body: Each produces structured risks: cause, probability, impact, evidence.

steps.title: The engine calculates
steps.body: Probability × impact, each scored 1 to 5. The same data always gives the same score: the calculation does not go through the AI.

steps.title: The auditor checks
steps.body: Contradictions, calculations, sources. Anything unsupported is sent back.

steps.title: You decide
steps.body: Summary, risk matrix, scenarios, mitigation plan. The platform recommends; it never acts on your behalf.

epistemic.title: You always know where a piece of information comes from.
epistemic.intro: An estimate is never presented as a fact. Every item in the report carries one of these four labels.

items.name: Verified fact
items.body: Sourced and dated. Example: the fixed peg between the CFA franc and the euro.

items.name: Estimate
items.body: Calculated, with its method and input data.

items.name: Assumption
items.body: Plausible but unconfirmed: check it before you decide.

items.name: AI lead
items.body: An idea suggested by an agent. Useful to think with, not to be taken as certain.

items.title: Hosted in Paris
items.body: Application and database inside the European Union.

items.title: Strict separation
items.body: Each company's data is kept apart down to the database. Tests check it on every update.

items.title: Audit trail
items.body: Sign-ins, invitations, role changes: every sensitive action is logged.

items.title: People decide
items.body: No decision is ever executed automatically. Recommendations stay recommendations.

cta.title: Got an important decision coming up?
cta.body: We are opening DecisionGuard to a first group of companies in Europe and Africa. Bring us a real file and we will analyse it with you.

footer.tagline: Risk analysis before decisions, for companies in Europe and Africa.

roles.title: One decision, three ways of looking at it.
roles.intro: The risks that worry a CEO are not the ones that keep a CFO up at night. DecisionGuard starts from your role.

list.scope: Entering a new country, acquisitions, launching an offer, strategic partnerships.
points: What the decision commits you to over three to five years
The dependencies you create: a supplier, a partner, a country
The signals to watch once the decision is made
list.example: Should we buy our distributor in Senegal?

list.scope: Investment, financing, cash flow, currency exposure.
points: Cash needs, and what happens if the budget slips
Currency exposure, including CFA franc, naira or cedi
What the file still lacks before you can decide
list.example: Should we fund the new warehouse with a loan?

list.scope: Cloud migration, choosing a vendor, a new application, compliance work.
points: Vendor lock-in, and how hard it would be to switch
GDPR duties and local data-protection laws
list.example: Move our ERP to a host outside Europe?

compare.title: What changes in the way you decide.
rows: Assumptions stay in the heads of whoever built the file.
Every assumption is written down and labelled, and you know which ones to confirm.
Risks are scored by gut feeling, differently from one meeting to the next.
The same calculation for every decision, so scores can be compared.
Each department looks at its own area and finds out about the others too late.
Finance, legal, cyber and operations in one file, including the risks that trigger each other.
Once the decision is made, the file goes into the archive.
The file can stay under watch and flag what has changed.
